::: {.finding}
Every public action on GitHub, a push, a star, a pull request, a comment, lands in a public log.
From {{n:window_start}} to {{n:window_end}} we read all of it: {{n:total_events}} events over
{{n:complete_days}} complete days.
:::

::: {.finding}
**A typical day brings about {{n:typical_day}} events,** from about {{n:typical_actors}}
accounts working in about {{n:typical_repos}} repositories.
:::

{{fig:gist}}

::: {.callout-flagged}
Shaded days had at least one hour where the public log itself was broken: far too few events,
or pushes missing. Those hours are left out of every average on these pages, and shown, never
hidden. The last page explains how we know.
:::

::: {.finding}
**Most of what happens is code being pushed:** pushes are {{n:push_share}} of all events.
**Robots do real work too:** about {{n:bot_share}} of events come from automated accounts.
:::
